title: Bind the shared 12-condition completion predicate to a workflow artifact
mechanism: single-reducer binding of the program completion predicate to the workflow type
question: Instantiate the program's single completion predicate (spec conditions 1-12) for the workflow-artifact type and emit a per-workflow CERTIFIED / PROVISIONAL / REJECTED record naming which of the 12 conditions passed, failed, or are not-applicable with a reason. Question: which of the 12 conditions are genuinely inapplicable to a workflow blueprint (versus quietly skipped), and does the same reducer run in the local runner, the tournament runner, and the certification gate?
answer: None of the 12 spec conditions are genuinely inapplicable to a workflow blueprint. Quiet skip is forbidden: a missing test, reviewer, mutation control, sentinel, manifest row, or downstream read is FAIL, not N/A. The reducer can still render N/A when unit_class is not workflow-artifact and the caller supplies applicability=false WITH a reason; N/A is never counted as a pass (golden-with-N/A on C9 yields CERTIFIED with pass_count=11 na_count=1). Unreasoned N/A fail-closes. The same reducer tools.foundry.completion_predicate.evaluate is imported by the local runner, the tournament runner, and the certification gate; the import graph is computed from AST (not asserted) and a planted rival predicate at the gate makes the detector fire.

answers.inapplicable_to_workflow_blueprint: None. All 12 conditions are applicable to workflow-artifact certification. Treating any as N/A would be a quiet skip of the spec. The applicability table records applicable=true and quietly_skipped=false for every condition.
answers.same_reducer_three_sites: Yes. AST import graph shows tools.foundry.completion_predicate imported and evaluate() called from tools/foundry/local_runner.py, tools/foundry/tournament_runner.py, and tools/foundry/certification_gate.py. The three sites return identical per-condition statuses on the same subject; only locus differs.

applicability.name: process/task reached a valid terminal state
applicability.reason: Certification of a blueprint is a process; a non-terminal run is not a certified workflow.

applicability.name: expected artifact exists
applicability.reason: The blueprint file must exist on disk; a path in the subject is not proof.

applicability.name: artifact is non-empty and exceeds a meaningful minimum size
applicability.reason: An empty or stub blueprint is not a workflow artifact; size is a real floor.

applicability.name: artifact parses against its schema
applicability.reason: The blueprint must parse against the workflow schema; invalid JSON is not certified.

applicability.name: required sentinel is present
applicability.reason: The certification sentinel is the stamp on the artifact, not a work-unit decoration.

applicability.name: required evidence anchors exist
applicability.reason: Two independent evidence anchors (file:line and a rerunnable command) are required.

applicability.name: required tests ran and passed
applicability.reason: Required tests must have run and passed; missing tests fail closed.

applicability.name: negative controls or mutations fail as expected
applicability.reason: Mutation controls must fire; a silent control is not evidence the gate is wired.

applicability.name: independent reviewer status is PASS
applicability.reason: Independent reviewer PASS is required; absence is FAIL, not a quiet N/A skip.

applicability.name: no unresolved P0/P1 defect is attached
applicability.reason: An unresolved P0/P1 attached to the workflow blocks certification.

applicability.name: output was registered in the artifact manifest
applicability.reason: The live sha256 must appear in the manifest; a plausible digest is not a receipt.

applicability.name: downstream consumers can read it
applicability.reason: A foundry consumer must actually read the blueprint; schema-ok is not enough.

source_inputs_on_this_tree.note: Catalog inputs are Windows harness-restore paths absent on this worktree. The 12-condition list is the catalog-quoted spec (CC-0003 / IMP-0415 / WFA-0042 extract of lines 10631-10644). CC-0003 / agentspec.oracle.judge is not on this tree; this module is the workflow-artifact instantiation, not a second program-wide oracle.
